summary: macOS native preflight on Darwin x86_64 passed all three native gates for snapshot 49b7d80811a03d4b3f54bd8191fc182469b33f81 (tree 555152ed6d000628dcddfce613569a78f08a563e). This is a git stash snapshot that bun run preflight:mac made of e32476594bace82b57980fe8e1d57e48e3c4c53c plus the working tree's tracked edits; it is not a branch commit, and it is not e32476594bace82b57980fe8e1d57e48e3c4c53c itself. The snapshot includes the final refused-connection test design: the OS refusal is injected into the real error mapping, because macOS times out a connection to a bound, never-listening port. The same rust/, scripts/, and evals/ files passed the Linux native preflight and a 40-run loop of the library tests. It qualifies only that snapshot on that Intel Mac; arm64, scope acceptance, and a committed candidate are missing.

results.behavior: On the Mac, check:rust passed in 186.4 s: cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace (1259 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored across 28 targets; the ignored test is the live CLIProxyAPI home test), and build. Within it the session target passed 174 tests including all 12 writer_exclusion tests (killed and exited holder processes taken over), bake-cli's a_held_session_is_refused passed, and both cliproxyapi::fetch::tests::a_refused_connection_asks_for_the_url_again and says_which_field_to_ask_again_and_words_each_failure passed. Counts in the command describe gates.

rust-pty passed with 20 preview PTY cases and 2 skipped (the two coalesced-resize barrier cases need Linux /proc process state). rust-eval passed 14 lines: the 4 native fixture cases (tamper-tests, claim-only, and edit-exit1 rejected) and the native bake-rs arm smoke on darwin x64 (8 samples, 22 requests, evaluator ~/.agents isolation, stray context-file refusal).

The refused-connection case no longer acquires a port: no loopback port can be held refusing on every OS (a freed port can be taken by any process on the host, and macOS times out a never-listening bound socket). fetch.rs now reads any error chain in transport_detail and builds the unreachable error in unreachable_error, both private and behavior-preserving; the test passes an io::ErrorKind::ConnectionRefused inside an error chain shaped like reqwest's and asserts the exact field, "Could not reach 127.0.0.1:4141 (ECONNREFUSED)", the message, and that the key is never quoted. Redirect, timeout, 401, 403, 404, other status, and non-JSON cases still run against a real loopback server. On Linux the native preflight passed (1285 Cargo tests, 1 ignored) and 40 of 40 library test runs passed. The earlier 16 of 40 and 0 of 40 loops in 2026-10-14-foundation-native-checks describe the candidate and the first fix, not this design.

negativeControls.defect: transport_detail appended the client error's own line, which names the URL and, in the test chain, the key.
negativeControls.assertion: a_refused_connection_asks_for_the_url_again failed on the exact text, which showed the leaked key (exit 101).
